title: AI Gamedev workflow
author: bstreak156
selftext:
Hello Everyone,

I have an idea of the game on which direction do we need to go. I have a base character finalised in an image however I’m not sure what is the best workflow for a game dev.

Some of my questions:  
How do we generate character animations?  
How do we equip accessories for the base character?

comments.author: FreeEye5
comments.body: Need lots more information my friend. 2d, 3d, isometric? Art style? Type of game? Types of movement?

replies.author: bstreak156
replies.body:
I’m working on a Telegram Mini App game and wanted feedback on the best way to approach it. The idea is a 2D real-time 1v1 battle game where players get matched with other online players in the same level range, and each match lasts around 60 seconds. The controls would be simple — left/right movement plus actions like punch, kick, equipping weapons, and using them during the fight.

For the first version, I want to keep it Telegram-native and launch it as a closed alpha inside a Mini App, since Telegram Mini Apps are basically web apps that run directly inside Telegram. Right now I only have concept art for the base character, so the art and animation pipeline is still open.

 The goal is to mix viral mechanics with actual skill-based combat and progression, so things like stamina, energy, rewards, upgrades, clans, and long-term progression are part of the plan.

On the economy side, I want rewards and assets to be on-chain, with NFTs giving stat boosts, progression advantages, and upgrade paths. Upgrades could come from chests or NFT shop purchases, while gameplay itself would still need to feel fair and fast.

comments.author: AdeptTrip2421
comments.body:
for character animations in a game pipeline, you'll want to look at sprite sheet generation or skeletal animation depending on your art style. if it's 2d, tools like Spine or DragonBones let you rig a base character and swap accessories as separate layers on the skeleton. for 3d, Mixamo handles animation retargeting pretty well once you have a rigged model.


Mage Space has a guide called Motion Control for AI Influencers that covers keeping consistent appearance across poses, which could help with your base character iterations
